title: Regenerative Nodes and Demand-Anchored Carbon Corridors: From Voluntary Offtake to Compliance in Singapore
content: Singapore has built Southeast Asia’s clearest compliance market for international carbon credits, yet eligible nature-based supply has barely formed. Projects cannot be financed until host countries authorise exports, and buyers will not contract until credits are eligible; as of November 2025, no credits had been purchased under Singapore’s International Carbon Credits framework. This paper proposes a demand-anchored structure to break that deadlock. A price band anchored to Singapore’s carbon tax gives buyers and sellers a public ceiling; a Compliance Step-Up Offtake lets buyers contract now at a voluntary price that steps up when credits become eligible; and a Regenerative Demand Note, backed by multilateral first-loss capital, turns signed demand into upfront restoration finance. Corridor sites, or regenerative nodes, pair mangroves and other nature assets with Singapore’s energy, food and water imports, with community trusts as contract parties. Scenario modelling sizes Singapore’s compliance-anchored demand at 3.2–3.8 MtCO2e a year to 2030, worth about S$110–170 million a year, and about 37 Mt over 2026–2035 in the base case. A review of precedent market structures finds that none yet combines a compliance price anchor, a route to authorisation, finance before eligibility and communities as contract parties. The paper proposes a council of the parties to steward shared rules, shows how a shared ledger and insurers can extend the market, and sets out twenty-one hypotheses and a research agenda for validation.
